items.title: Tom McIntosh — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We had a wonderful teacher; her name was Mrs. Williams, Mildred Williams.

ctx.x: I was going to ask you something else about growing up.

Okay well, my recollection leads me to the fact that when we went to junior high school, there was no music program. We had a wonderful teacher; her name was Mrs. Williams, Mildred Williams. She saw the situation and decided to turn things around. The first thing she did was to invite a high school orchestra from Washington, the Cardozo high school, all black. I was stunned to see kids my age, 14 or 15 years of age, playing music and it sounded the best. Because they were coming out of Spanish circumstances, they…
very talented. He could play the piano. We went to the same church, and then we became the M&M quartet. So, that was really my first stab at performing music.
